bugs.summary: With center set, under/over are always copied from the original cmap even when the user never set them, so a cmap with default extremes gets its out-of-range colours pinned to the original cmap's end colours instead of the recentred cmap's end colours.
bugs.evidence: seaborn/matrix.py:223-224 'under = self.cmap(-np.inf)' / 'over = self.cmap(np.inf)' (for an unset extreme matplotlib returns the cmap's end colour) and 231-232 unconditional 'self.cmap.set_under(under)' / 'set_over(over)' on the ListedColormap built from self.cmap(cc), whose ends are cmap(cmin)/cmap(cmax). Fix commit 5893daa adds 'under_set = under != self.cmap(0)', 'over_set = over != self.cmap(self.cmap.N - 1)' and sets each only when set.

bugs.summary: The new test's over-colour block without center asserts cmap(-np.inf) == hm.cmap(-np.inf), the under value, so the uncentred over-colour case is never checked.
bugs.evidence: seaborn/tests/test_matrix.py:234 'cmap.set_over("red")' then 237 'npt.assert_array_equal(cmap(-np.inf), hm.cmap(-np.inf))'; the matching centred block at 241 uses np.inf and the under block at 230 uses -np.inf.

rejected.was: 18: 'import copy' placed out of alphabetical order
R2 22-medium: test uses mpl.cm.get_cmap, removed in matplotlib 3.9
rejected.why: Not a defect of this change: get_cmap was the supported API when the PR merged (2020) and the module already uses it; later upstream deprecation is not introduced here.
